title: How Exceptional Teachers Improve Listening https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2013/09/28/how-exceptional-teachers-improve-listening/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes listening as a near-obsession among exceptional teachers and introduces the 'post-direction strategy' for strengthening it. Rather than jumping in with reminders or rephrasing the moment students appear confused after a direction, teachers allow them to struggle and search their own memory for what was asked, intervening only if students are truly out of options—at which point the exact same direction is repeated, not simplified. He distinguishes this from behavior problems, which should be addressed immediately rather than allowed to play out. The strategy is framed as restoring students' confidence that they need only listen once, gradually eliminating the culture of constant reminders that erodes listening over time.
points: Listening is described as the foundational skill exceptional teachers obsess over, since nothing else in the classroom goes as planned without it.
The 'post-direction strategy' means allowing students to struggle and search their memory after a direction rather than immediately rephrasing or reminding.
If intervention becomes necessary, the teacher repeats the exact same direction rather than simplifying or hinting, sending a stronger message.
The strategy applies only to genuine listening struggles, not misbehavior or students who aren't earnestly trying, which should be stopped immediately.
Consistent use of the strategy is intended to restore students' confidence that they are capable of listening once and don't need repeated reminders.
quotes: If you were to break down what makes exceptional teachers so effective, you would find their ability to teach students to listen one of several key common traits.
It is listening, they will reveal to you in quiet-corner conversation, where the secrets of great teaching can be found.
The way the post-direction strategy works is that instead of jumping in to help at the first sign of trouble, you will allow them to struggle.
Now it’s important to note that if your students are in any way misbehaving or are otherwise not earnestly trying to follow your directions, you should stop them immediately.
Listening deteriorates in an environment of incessant reminding and hint-giving.
The post-direction strategy gives them tangible proof that they need only listen to your directions once, that they are capable and self-reliant
